description: utopia-php/validators: request parameter validators, their descriptions and types.

validator.new.doc: new Utopia\Validator\<class>(...$args): a handle (validators in args: handles or specs)

validator.is_valid.doc: $validator->isValid($value); the handle remembers what getDescription() reports afterwards

validator.description.doc: $validator->getDescription(), after the handle's earlier isValid() calls

validator.get.doc: a getter by property: validators, validator (as {description, type}), bits, unsigned, format, min, max, list

validator.check.doc: a fresh validator from a spec: isValid($value), then getDescription(): {valid, description}

validator.sequence.doc: one validator from a spec: isValid() then getDescription() for each of `values` in turn (state across calls)

waivers.Utopia\\Validator\\PHPStan\\DisallowAsse: PHPStan extension for the package's own tests: no runtime behaviour

tests_waived.packages/validators/tests/CompatTest.php: class aliases for the names before the rename (Utopia\Validator, Utopia\PHPStan\DisallowAssertEqualsExtension) and PHPStan's extension: PHP autoloading plumbing; Rust has one Validator trait, which third-party validators implement (crates/utopia/validators tests)

quirks.description: the allow list is checked with a loose in_array(): numeric strings compare as numbers, so allowList ['01'] accepts '1'
a loose list compares lower-cased strings with ==: numeric strings compare as numbers ('1e3' accepts '1000', '0.0' accepts 0 and false)
the pattern has no D modifier: $ also matches before a final newline, so 'fff\n' is valid
quirks.case: edge.json#Patterns without D accept a final newline (quirk)

quirks.description: the pattern has no D modifier: '+1234567\n' is valid
quirks.case: edge.json#Phone without D accepts a final newline (quirk)

quirks.description: empty($value) rejects the string '0' (even with allowEmpty)
the description reads 'Value must a valid array' (no 'be')
a value json_encode() cannot encode (INF, invalid UTF-8) counts as 0 bytes (strlen(false)), so it passes the length limit
quirks.case: edge.json#Assoc counts a failed json_encode as 0 bytes

quirks.description: a restriction with levels PHP_INT_MAX overflows $levels + 1 to a float, which explode() rejects with TypeError

deviations.php: $length and $min are int: a negative $length rejects every string and a negative $min is described as 'at least -1 chars'
deviations.reason: Rust lengths are usize: a negative length or minimum is unrepresentable (the PHP behaviour is nonsense)

deviations.php: $type is any string, returned by getType(); likewise AnyOf, NoneOf, Multiple (where null makes getType() throw TypeError), WhiteList and Range's $format (any value other than integer or double rejects every value)
deviations.reason: Rust takes a Type, one of the Validator::TYPE_* constants; other strings are not types

deviations.php: $patterns is an untyped array: patterns are cast with (string) when used (an int pattern matches its digits, a stdClass throws Error, an array is 'Array' with a warning)
deviations.reason: Rust patterns are strings; callers cast. Likewise the string lists of Globstar, Host, Hostname (string[]), URL's $allowedSchemes, Text's $allowList (string[]) and Domain restrictions, which are built by Domain::createRestriction (typed)

deviations.php: the list keeps the keys it was given; a loose list keeps them on its lower-cased values
deviations.reason: Rust lists are sequences: keys are dropped (isValid() and getDescription() ignore them in PHP too)

deviations.php: AllOf, AnyOf, NoneOf and JSON\FCM keep state between calls: getDescription() reads what decided the last isValid() that decided (the failed rule, kept by AllOf and NoneOf through later successful calls, or FCM's error), evaluated now: a deciding rule that is itself stateful (JSON\FCM, a composite) and is validated again in a later call that the composite does not decide reports its new state
deviations.reason: Rust validators are shared by concurrent requests and stateless: validate() returns the decision as data (Verdict::decided, Verdict::rule and the description PHP reports), and a caller replaying PHP's sequence keeps the latest decision (the adapter does, per handle). The description a kept decision reported is not recomputed from the deciding rule's later validations
